body.statement: Every two real closed fields satisfy the same first-order sentences in the language of ordered fields.  In particular, a first-order sentence with rational coefficients holds over \(\mathbb R\) if and only if it holds over the real algebraic closure of \(\mathbb Q\).

source.locator: Quantifier-elimination theorem for real closed fields
source.verbatim_statement: The elementary theory of real closed fields is complete: every first-order sentence in the language of ordered fields has the same truth value in every real closed field. Consequently a sentence with rational coefficients holds in the real numbers if and only if it holds in the field of real algebraic numbers.

attestation.note: Transcribed as the direct transfer consequence of Tarski, A Decision Method for Elementary Algebra and Geometry (1951), quantifier-elimination theorem; RAND/University of California Press source record consulted.
